core_obligations: The horizontal maps (proof lines 3440-3443): the two maps between the cohomology groups in each degree are the ones induced by the maps of complexes, using that cohomology is a functor.

The boundary map (proof lines 3443-3457): the connecting morphism from the cohomology of the third complex to the cohomology of the first in the next degree is taken to be the map produced by the snake lemma applied to the displayed commutative diagram whose rows are the cokernels of the previous differentials and the kernels of the next ones.

Identifications and exactness (proof lines 3457-3463): the kernel of the right vertical map in that diagram is the cohomology of the third complex and the cokernel of the left vertical map is the cohomology of the first complex in the next degree, and the exactness of the long sequence is part (2) of the snake lemma.
Functoriality and shifts (proof lines 3463-3465): functoriality is the naturality statement for the snake lemma's connecting map, and compatibility with shifts is immediate from the definitions.
proof_roadmap: Take the horizontal maps from functoriality of cohomology.
Apply the snake lemma to the diagram of cokernels and kernels to build the boundary map.
Identify the outer terms with cohomology and read exactness off the snake lemma, then handle functoriality and shifts.
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces the long exact cohomology sequence attached to a short exact sequence of cochain complexes, compatible with shifts (statement lines 3406-3438). The proof is a complete argument: the horizontal maps come from functoriality of cohomology, the connecting map is obtained by applying the snake lemma to an explicitly displayed diagram of cokernels and kernels (proof lines 3440-3457), the two outer terms of that diagram are identified with the cohomology groups so that the exactness statement of the snake lemma gives the exactness of the long sequence (proof lines 3457-3463), and functoriality and shift compatibility are disposed of by a named naturality result and by the definitions (proof lines 3463-3465). The non-formal content is the choice of the diagram to which the snake lemma is applied. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
